kw.doc: Load the bench, its calibration and the radio file, and prepare the instruments. All five are mandatory and differ from tester to tester, so suites take them from the command line (-v BENCH:... and so on). `firmware` names what the radio runs, such as a git describe; `hardware` names the unit, by model and serial number, since units of one model measure differently. `dsp` names the DSP image the radio's audio processor runs, such as its sha256; it is mandatory for radio files with dsp_image: true, whose firmware states can differ in it alone.

kw.doc: Step the level down from `start` to `stop` until fewer than half get through: for kind=stream a `frames`-long stream at each level, counting frames decoded (and garbled frames played); for kind=sms `frames` SMS, counting those intact. The result has the curve and the levels where 90% and 50% still got through, interpolated. Levels are dBm at the radio with a transmitter level table (or absolute: true), otherwise dB relative to the bench's gain: compare relative results only within one session, on one bench. Takes Score M17 Stream's or Score M17 SMS's options.

kw.name: Close Bench
kw.doc: Stop the instruments and write measurements.json: every capture, check and operator answer, with the run's provenance. Absolute paths are made relative, so the file can be published as it is.

suite.doc:
M17 receive, read from the radio's own trace: a trace build of OpenRTX (firmware/m17-trace) reports every frame it decodes on its USB serial port (the bench's trace section), so each frame the transmitter sends is accounted for without an operator: decoded, missed, garbled or repeated, when the link setup data arrived and from where, which frames went to the speaker, and the receive thread's stack.
Flash a trace build of the firmware under test. The measurements are of the radio's ordinary M17 receive: the trace only copies out what the decoder hands on. Levels are relative to the bench's gain unless ABSOLUTE_LEVELS is true and the calibration has a transmitter level table; relative results compare firmware only within one session on one bench. Tag "long" marks the soak.
